licoes.objectivo: Abrir, sinalizar e fechar uma apresentação com marcadores de discurso formal.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I'd like to start by [looking] at last year's results.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: [Moving] on to the costs, option B is cheaper.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: This [brings] me to the most important part.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: [To sum] up, option A is safer.

exercicios.enunciado: Which is the best way to open a presentation?

opcoes.texto: The purpose of this presentation is to show you our new plan.
Sorry, I have a lot of slides.

exercicios.enunciado: "Subsequently" means…
Which phrase introduces the most important point?

opcoes.texto: This brings me to the most important part.

exercicios.enunciado: "Resumindo, …" numa apresentação. Em inglês:
Gostaria de começar por olhar para os números.
exercicios.resposta: I'd like to start by looking at the figures.

exercicios.frase: I'm Nuno. I'd like to start by looking at what happened in Namibe. Then I'll move on to our two options.
exercicios.enunciado: What will Nuno talk about first?

exercicios.frase: This is Lerato. Never apologise for your slides, and tell the board the parts of your talk first.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Lerato tell Nuno not to do?

exercicios.frase: Moving on to… the costs.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com uma pausa curta depois de "Moving on to".
Open a presentation about your company, your department, your course or your town: who you are, the purpose, three parts in order, and then move to the first part.
exercicios.frase: The purpose of this presentation
exercicios.resposta: Good morning. My name is Teresa Gomes, from the training department. The purpose of this presentation is to show you our new training plan. I'd like to start by looking at last year's results. Then I'll move on to the new courses, and finally, the budget. So, to begin with, the results.

exercicios.enunciado: In your opinion, what makes a presentation boring? And what makes it interesting?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: A presentation is boring when the speaker reads the slides, because the audience can read too. It's interesting when there's a story, a few clear numbers and a speaker who looks at people.

licoes.objectivo: Descrever gráficos e tendências com verbos, nomes, adjectivos e advérbios.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Sales [rose] sharply in March.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: There was a [sharp] fall in December.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: The downtime fell [sharply] in November.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: It peaked in September, [at] thirty-eight hours.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Prices rose [by] ten percent, from 200 to 220 kwanzas.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: The number of customers rose from 1 000 [to] 1 600 in April.

exercicios.enunciado: "It fell slightly" means…
After a big fall, the number stayed almost the same for months. It…
Choose the correct sentence.

exercicios.frase: I'm Nuno. In November, the satellite started working, and the downtime fell sharply, to twelve hours.
exercicios.enunciado: What happened in November?

opcoes.texto: The downtime fell sharply, to twelve hours.
The downtime rose to twelve hours.

exercicios.frase: This is Elsa. The downtime peaked in September, at thirty-eight hours. That was the month of the sandstorm.
exercicios.enunciado: When was the peak?

exercicios.frase: There was an increase. Prices increased.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita: o nome com o acento na primeira sílaba, o verbo na segunda.
Describe this chart in English: "Alunos por mês, escola de línguas, Huambo, 2028: Jan 120; Fev 125; Mar 130; Abr 210 (anúncio na rádio); Mai 215; Jun 140 (férias); Jul 135; Ago 180."
exercicios.frase: rose
exercicios.resposta: The chart shows the number of students at a language school in Huambo in 2028. From January to March, it rose steadily, from 120 to 130. In April, there was a sharp rise, to 210, after a radio advert. It peaked in May, then fell sharply in June, because of the holidays, and rose again in August.

exercicios.enunciado: Do you prefer to read numbers in a table or in a chart? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: I prefer a chart, because I can see the trend in a second. But for exact numbers, like a budget, a table is better. The best presentations have a chart on the slide and the table in the handout.

licoes.objectivo: Usar o future perfect para metas e prazos.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: By the end of March, we [will have laid] all the cables.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: We [won't have] finished the control room by May.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: By the time the plant [opens], we'll have tested the network.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: [By] June, we'll have installed the antennas.

exercicios.enunciado: "Até Junho (o mais tardar), teremos instalado as antenas." Em inglês:

opcoes.texto: By June, we will have installed the antennas.
Until June, we will have installed the antennas.
By June, we will installed the antennas.

exercicios.enunciado: Which sentence is about an action finished before a moment in the future?

opcoes.texto: By August, we'll have tested the network.
This time next year, we'll be finishing the control room.

exercicios.enunciado: "Will you have finished by Friday?" — "No, …"
Até ao fim do ano, teremos aberto a nova loja.
exercicios.resposta: By the end of the year, we'll have opened the new shop.

exercicios.frase: I'm Paulo. By the end of May, we'll have installed the antennas and the satellite, if they arrive on time.
exercicios.enunciado: What will they have done by the end of May?

opcoes.texto: installed the antennas and the satellite

exercicios.frase: This is Paulo. We won't have finished the control room by May. The building won't be ready until July.
exercicios.enunciado: Why won't the control room be finished by May?

opcoes.texto: The building won't be ready until July.

exercicios.frase: By May, we'll have installed everything.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita: "we'll have" curto.
Present one goal for your team or your studies, and say what will have happened by the end of the year — and one thing that won't have happened yet.
exercicios.frase: By the end of
exercicios.resposta: Our goal this year is to open a second shop in Lubango. By the end of October, we'll have found the place, and by November, we'll have hired three people. By the end of the year, we'll have sold our first products there. But we won't have paid back the loan.

exercicios.enunciado: Is it better to promise an early deadline and work hard, or a later deadline you are sure about? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: A later deadline you're sure about, because a missed deadline destroys trust. If you finish early, the client is happy. If you promise early and finish late, they remember only the delay.

licoes.objectivo: Responder a perguntas do público: ganhar tempo, reformular, admitir e prometer voltar.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I'll get [back] to you on that by Friday.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I'm [afraid] I don't have that figure with me.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: So, if I [understand] correctly, you're asking about the costs.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Does that [answer] your question?

exercicios.enunciado: You don't know the exact figure. The best answer:

opcoes.texto: I'm afraid I don't have that figure with me. I'll get back to you on that by Friday.
Er… maybe two thousand? Or three?

exercicios.enunciado: Someone asks about the costs, but your costs slide comes later. You say:

opcoes.texto: Can I come back to that at the end? I'll cover it in the costs section.
I don't want to answer that.

exercicios.enunciado: "Vou dar-lhe uma resposta sobre isso até sexta." Em inglês:

opcoes.texto: I'll get back to you on that by Friday.
I'll return you the answer until Friday.
I'll give you a feedback until Friday.

exercicios.enunciado: Why is "So, if I understand correctly, you're asking…" useful?

opcoes.texto: You check the question, and you get time to think.

exercicios.enunciado: Deixe-me pensar nisso por um momento.
exercicios.resposta: Let me think about that for a moment.

exercicios.frase: I'm Sílvia. Why should we pay nine hundred dollars a month for a satellite we hardly use?
exercicios.enunciado: What is Sílvia's question about?

opcoes.texto: the monthly cost of the satellite

exercicios.frase: This is Lerato. Don't guess. A wrong number is much worse than "I'll get back to you".
exercicios.enunciado: What is Lerato's advice?

exercicios.frase: That's a good question. Let me think about that for a moment.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com a voz calma e a descer.

You presented a plan to move your office. A colleague asks: "Why move now? The rent is going up, and nobody wants to travel further." Answer: gain time, check the question, give two reasons, and check your answer.
exercicios.frase: That's a good question
exercicios.resposta: That's a good question. So, you're asking why we're moving now, when it costs more. First, our building has no parking, which means clients arrive late. Second, the new one is next to the bus station, so most of us will travel less. Does that answer your question?

exercicios.enunciado: In a meeting, someone asks you what the training will cost next year. You don't know. Answer politely and promise to come back with the figure.
exercicios.frase: get back to you
exercicios.resposta: Thank you for asking. I'm afraid I don't have next year's figure with me, because the school is still preparing the prices. I'll check with them and get back to you on that by Thursday.

licoes.objectivo: Palavras de diapositivos e dados, números aproximados, ênfase; graphic e adequate.

exercicios.enunciado: Ligue cada palavra à tradução.
Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I'd like to [draw] your attention to this figure.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: [On] average, the plant loses less than an hour a month.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Thirty-one hours is just [over] thirty.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Nineteen percent is just [under] twenty percent.

exercicios.enunciado: "O gráfico mostra as vendas." Em inglês:
exercicios.explicacao: Falso amigo: graphic = visual, de design, ou chocante.

exercicios.enunciado: "uma solução adequada para a central" em inglês:

opcoes.texto: a suitable solution for the plant
an adequate solution for the plant
an adequated solution for the plant

exercicios.explicacao: Falso amigo: adequate = suficiente, mas só à justa.

exercicios.enunciado: "The budget is adequate." This means…
About 26 people out of 100:

exercicios.frase: I'm Nuno. On average, the plant now loses less than an hour a month.
exercicios.enunciado: How much downtime does the plant have now, on average?

opcoes.texto: less than an hour a month

exercicios.frase: In December, the downtime fell to… one hour.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com uma pausa antes de "one hour".
Present one slide about your work, your studies or your town, with three numbers. Say what kind of chart it is, draw attention to one figure, and use approximate numbers.
exercicios.frase: draw your attention
exercicios.resposta: This pie chart shows how our students travel to school. Roughly half come by taxi, about a quarter walk, and just under twenty percent come by car. I'd like to draw your attention to this figure: only five percent come by bus. That's why we want a new bus line.

exercicios.enunciado: How many slides should a ten-minute presentation have? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: About eight, I think, because each slide needs at least a minute. With forty slides, the speaker runs and nobody remembers anything. One idea per slide is enough.

licoes.objectivo: Avaliar três aberturas de apresentações, com sotaques diferentes.

exercicios.frase: I'm Tobias. Sorry, I'm a bit nervous. I have forty-two slides, so I'll try to go fast.
exercicios.enunciado: How many slides does Tobias have?

exercicios.frase: This is Aïcha. This happened in my village, in Senegal, eleven years ago. That night, I decided to work in energy.
exercicios.enunciado: What did Aïcha decide that night?

exercicios.frase: I'm Aïcha. Today, I'd like to show you how forty villages now have power all night.
exercicios.enunciado: How many villages have power all night now?

exercicios.frase: This is Martin. Here's a number: thirty-seven percent. That's roughly how much power some plants lose before it reaches anyone's home.
exercicios.enunciado: What is Martin's first number?

exercicios.frase: I'm Nuno. Martin started well, but then I got lost. CAPEX, OPEX, LCOE… I didn't understand a word.
exercicios.enunciado: Why did Nuno get lost?

exercicios.frase: This is Lerato. Your board is the same: Celeste is a lawyer, not an engineer.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Lerato say about Celeste?

opcoes.texto: She's a lawyer, not an engineer.

exercicios.enunciado: Which opening was the strongest?

opcoes.texto: Aïcha's: a story, a pause, the purpose and the parts
Tobias's: an apology and forty-two slides
Martin's: a number and a lot of jargon

exercicios.enunciado: What was good about Martin's opening?

exercicios.frase: Imagine you are a nurse in a small clinic.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita em voz alta.

exercicios.frase: I'll start with the problem, move on to our solution, and finish with three lessons.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita em voz alta.
A colleague is going to speak at a conference. Tell them which of the three openings was the best, which was the worst, and give three pieces of advice.
exercicios.frase: The best opening
exercicios.resposta: The best opening was Aïcha's. She started with a story about a clinic, which made everyone listen, and then she gave the purpose and the three parts. The worst was Tobias: he apologised and had forty-two slides. My advice: start with a picture, give an outline, and avoid jargon.

exercicios.enunciado: Would you start a work presentation with a personal story? Why, or why not?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: Sometimes, yes, because people remember stories more than numbers. But it must be short and connected to the topic. For a very formal board, I'd start with one strong number instead.

exercicios.enunciado: Nuno opens with: "Imagine it's a Sunday in September, and a sandstorm hits your plant." Why?

opcoes.texto: to give the board a picture they'll remember
to talk about the weather forecast

opcoes.texto: Option A costs four hundred and twelve thousand dollars in total.
Option A costs four hundred twelve mil dollars in total.
Option A costs four hundreds and twelve thousands dollars.

exercicios.enunciado: The table says: "Instalação e obra: 96 000." Nuno rounds it:
The table says: "Custo mensal: opção A 2 400; opção B 1 500." What is the difference, and why?

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.

I'm Ingrid. In Namibe, the antennas were stuck in customs. Will you really have installed everything by May?

opcoes.texto: how many local people will work on the installation

Present a proposal of your own (work, school or community): an opening with a picture or a number, the purpose, one figure, one deadline with the future perfect, and a recommendation.
exercicios.frase: recommend
exercicios.resposta: Imagine forty students waiting in the sun for a taxi. That's our school today. The purpose of this talk is to propose a school bus. Roughly half of our students spend over an hour going home. By March, we'll have bought the bus. To sum up, we recommend it, and we'd like your approval today.

exercicios.enunciado: Explain this table to an English-speaking colleague, without reading every line: "Duas viaturas para a equipa. Modelo X: 32 000 000 Kz, 9 litros aos 100 km, garantia de 3 anos. Modelo Y: 26 500 000 Kz, 12 litros aos 100 km, garantia de 1 ano."
exercicios.frase: Model
exercicios.resposta: We have two cars for the team. Model X costs thirty-two million kwanzas, uses nine litres per hundred kilometres, and has a three-year guarantee. Model Y is about five and a half million cheaper, but it uses more fuel, and the guarantee is only one year.
exercicios.contexto: Mediação: o total, o que muda e o mais importante.

licoes.objectivo: Rever a unidade 2 do B2 e reciclar a unidade 1 do B2 e as unidades 8 e 10 do B1.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I'd like to finish by [thanking] my team.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: The price of bread rose [slightly], from 300 to 310 kwanzas.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: By next March, I [will have finished] my course.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: [By] the time you arrive, we'll have eaten.

exercicios.enunciado: Choose the correct sentence.
You don't know the answer to a question. The best reply:

opcoes.texto: I'm afraid I don't have that information with me. I'll get back to you by Monday.
Maybe. I don't know. Next question.

exercicios.enunciado: Reciclagem (B2, unidade 1). Choose the correct sentence.

opcoes.texto: Celeste, who is a lawyer, chairs the board.
Celeste, that is a lawyer, chairs the board.
Celeste who is a lawyer, chairs the board.

exercicios.enunciado: Reciclagem (B1, unidade 10). "Ele devia ter dito que não sabia." Em inglês:

opcoes.texto: He should have said he didn't know.
He should said he didn't know.
He must have say he didn't know.

exercicios.enunciado: Reciclagem (B1, unidade 8). Complete: "This time next year, we'll ___ the control room."
Isto leva-me à parte mais importante.
exercicios.resposta: This brings me to the most important part.

exercicios.frase: This is Paulo. By the time the plant opens, we'll have tested the network for three months.
exercicios.enunciado: For how long will they have tested the network?
Present a plan: open it, describe one figure with a trend, give one deadline with the future perfect, and close with a recommendation.
exercicios.frase: To sum up
exercicios.resposta: Good morning. The purpose of this talk is to propose a weekly English class. Last year, our client calls in English rose sharply, by forty percent. By June, we'll have trained twenty people. To sum up, we recommend one class a week, and we'd like your approval today.

exercicios.enunciado: At the end of your presentation, someone asks: "Isn't this too expensive?" Gain time, check the question, answer, and check your answer.
exercicios.frase: Does that answer your question
exercicios.resposta: That's a fair question. So, you're asking if the cost is too high. It costs about two thousand dollars a year, which is less than one lost client. And we'll see the results by June. Does that answer your question?
